newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - M&S profits hit record, adds 1,700 jobs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - M&S profits hit record, adds 1,700 jobs.

text.p: Britain's biggest clothing retailer Marks and Spencer Plc said it would create 1,700 new jobs in Britain after reporting record profits for last year of more than one billion pounds ($1.6 billion).

The retailer, which now has stores in Europe, North America and Asia, will spend 1.5 billion pounds over the next three years as part of its aggressive expansion overseas as well as adding space in Britain, where it already has 286 stores.
Chairman Sir Richard Greenbury said M&S had increased market share in Britain in clothing and held share in food despite fierce competition.
"It's a very, very competitive environment in clothing, in foods, in retailing generally. In every single area it's competitive," he told Reuters in an interview.

Marks, the retail sector leader, is one of the clear winners in the Britain's increasingly cut-throat retail market, where food superstores and clothing shops are waging a fierce battle for sales and profits.
Last year M&S's pretax profits rose 10.9 percent to 1.1 billion pounds ($1.8 billion), on sales up 8.7 percent to 7.84 billion. The total dividend was up 14 percent to 13 pence a share.
The group said in food, the British environment was fiercely competitive, but M&S held market share and maintained margins.
Greenbury said M&S had increased market share in clothing and home furnishing and held its share of the food market "to the decimal point".
"We posted a nine and half percent increase and national clothing sales in (the) same 52 weeks are 6.1 percent ahead...We've obviously gained market share," he said.
Greenbury said the extra British staff would not mean costs would rise faster than sales.

"People are concerned that when we take on extra staff the costs will rise faster than the sales but they haven't done that," he said. The return on sales last year was held at about 14 percent, which he said was one of the highest in the world.
He said he was not worried about the new Labour government's plans for a minimum wage, since M&S already paid staff more than the minimum being talked about.
"Whatever happens...if you include both the bonus at Christmas and the non contributory pension, we're paying over six pounds an hour."
The retailer will spend the bulk of the 1.5 billion pounds earmarked for expansion in Britain and continental Europe, including 30 or 40 sites in Germany, France and Spain.

Greenbury said that in Britain the group planned to add selling space by extending existing stores by 260,000 square feet, and opening new stores with a total of 200,000 square feet at Cribbs Causeway in Bristol and Newry in Northern Ireland.
There were still opportunities to expand in Britain even though M&S was in most town centres and most places on the edge of towns or outside them that it wanted to be.

He said M&S would be interested in buying stores put up for sale by retailing group Littlewoods LWD.CN, but M&S did not want to buy the entire business. "They've got one or two very interesting sites, but they're trying to sell the business as a going concern," he said.
The company's overseas businesses did well despite the strong pound, generating sales of 1.3 billion pounds, up nine percent and operating profits of 91 million, an increase of 23 percent.
But the group predicted that next year, based on current exchange rates, profits would be reduced by about 20 million pounds because of the strength of sterling.
Financial services, an increasingly important part of the group, contributed 76 million pounds to overall profit.
The group is also expanding its mail order business, and will begin a regional trial of clothing catalogues early next year.
Greenbury said its franchise operations, with outlets in 22 countries, was also performing strongly and said the group planned to develop new businesses in Poland and the Gulf states.
M&S shares slipped nine pence to 500 by midday. Traders said profit forecasts could be adjusted to take account of the impact of the strong pound.
($ = 0.608 British Pounds)
